description: Distributed version control system for tracking code changes.

git-init.title: Initialize repository
git-init.description: Creates a new empty Git repository in the current directory, generating the .git folder that stores the entire history.
examples: Initializes the repository in the current directory.
Creates the meu-projeto folder with the initial branch named main.
arguments: Sets the initial branch name (e.g. main).
Creates a repository without a working tree, used on servers.

git-clone.title: Clone repository
git-clone.description: Copies a remote repository to your machine, including the full history, and automatically sets up the origin remote.
examples: Clones the repository into the repo folder.
Shallow clone: downloads only the latest commit, useful for CI.
arguments: Limits history to the last n commits (shallow clone).
Directly clones a specific branch.

git-status.title: Check repository status
git-status.description: Shows the current branch, modified files, files staged for commit and untracked files.
examples: Shows the full state of the working tree.
Short format: one line per file (M, A, ??).
arguments: Short, compact output.
Shows the branch even in short format.

git-add.title: Add to staging
git-add.description: Moves changes to the staging area, marking them for inclusion in the next commit.
examples: Adds a specific file to staging.
Adds all changes in the current directory.
Interactive mode: choose hunk by hunk what goes into the commit.
arguments: Adds all changes, including deletions, across the whole repository.
Interactively selects the hunks to add.

git-reset-file.title: Unstage
git-reset-file.description: Removes a file from the staging area without discarding the changes in the file. Replaces the old git reset <file>.
examples: Unstages app.ts, keeping the edits.
arguments: Operates on the staging area (index) instead of the working tree.

git-restore.title: Discard local changes
git-restore.description: Undoes uncommitted changes to a file in the working tree, going back to the last committed state.
examples: Discards the unsaved changes in config.json.
Discards the changes in all tracked files.
arguments: Restores from a specific commit.
warnings: Discarded changes cannot be recovered, since they were never committed.

git-commit.title: Create commit
git-commit.description: Records the changes in the staging area into the repository history with a descriptive message.
examples: Creates a commit with the given message.
Stages already-tracked files and commits in one step.
arguments: Sets the commit message on the command line.
Automatically includes modified tracked files.

git-commit-amend.title: Amend last commit
git-commit-amend.description: Replaces the most recent commit, letting you change the message or include new staged changes.
examples: Rewrites the last commit's message.
Adds the staged changes to the last commit without changing the message.
arguments: Keeps the current message.
warnings: Rewrites the commit hash; never amend commits already pushed to a shared branch.

git-branch-list.title: List branches
git-branch-list.description: Lists local branches, highlighting the current branch with an asterisk.
examples: Lists local branches.
Lists local and remote branches.
arguments: Includes remote branches.
Shows only remote branches.

git-switch-create.title: Create and switch branch
git-switch-create.description: Creates a new branch from the current one and switches to it right away. A clearer alternative to git checkout -b.
examples: Creates and switches to the feature/login branch.
arguments: Creates the branch before switching.

git-switch.title: Switch branch
git-switch.description: Moves the working tree to another existing branch. Replaces using git checkout to switch branches.
examples: Goes back to the main branch.
Switches to the previous branch.
warnings: Uncommitted changes may block the switch; use git stash first if needed.

git-branch-delete.title: Delete branch
git-branch-delete.description: Removes an already-merged local branch. Use -D to force deletion of an unmerged branch.
examples: Deletes the branch if it has already been merged.
Forces deletion even without a merge (loses the unique commits).
arguments: Deletes only if the branch is merged.
Forces deletion (shortcut for --delete --force).
warnings: -D discards commits unique to the branch that exist nowhere else.

git-merge.title: Merge branch
git-merge.description: Integrates another branch's changes into the current branch, creating a merge commit when needed.
examples: Brings the commits from feature/login into the current branch.
Creates a merge commit even when a fast-forward would be possible.
arguments: Always creates a merge commit, preserving the branch history.
Cancels a conflicted merge and returns to the previous state.
warnings: May produce conflicts that must be resolved manually before finishing.

git-merge-abort.title: Abort conflicted merge
git-merge-abort.description: Stops an in-progress merge with conflicts and restores the branch to its pre-merge state.
examples: Undoes the conflicting merge.
warnings: Discards the conflict resolutions made so far.

git-rebase.title: Rebase branch
git-rebase.description: Reapplies the current branch's commits on top of another base, creating a linear history with no merge commits.
examples: Reapplies the current branch's commits on top of main.
Interactive rebase of the last 3 commits (reorder, squash, edit).
arguments: Interactive rebase: edit, reorder or combine commits.
Rebases onto a specific point.
warnings: Rewrites hashes; don't rebase commits already published on shared branches.

git-rebase-continue.title: Continue rebase after conflict
git-rebase-continue.description: Proceeds with the rebase after you resolve the conflicts and stage the files.
examples: Marks the conflicts as resolved and continues the rebase.
arguments: Cancels the rebase and returns to the initial state.
Skips the current conflicting commit.

git-remote-add.title: Add remote repository
git-remote-add.description: Links a remote repository to a short name (usually origin) for pushing and pulling changes.
examples: Sets origin as the main remote.
Lists the configured remotes and their URLs.
arguments: Shows the URLs (verbose) when listing.

git-fetch.title: Fetch remote changes
git-fetch.description: Downloads commits, branches and tags from the remote without touching your working tree or merging automatically.
examples: Updates origin's remote references.
Removes local references to branches that no longer exist on the remote.
arguments: Prunes remote branches that were deleted.
Fetches from all remotes.

git-pull.title: Update local branch
git-pull.description: Combines fetch and merge: fetches the remote's changes and integrates them into the current branch.
examples: Updates the current branch from the tracked remote.
Applies your local commits on top of the remote ones, avoiding a merge commit.
arguments: Uses rebase instead of merge to integrate.
warnings: May produce conflicts if the changes have diverged.

git-push.title: Push commits to remote
git-push.description: Sends the current branch's local commits to the corresponding remote repository.
examples: Pushes the current branch to the already-tracked remote.
Pushes and starts tracking origin/main as upstream.
arguments: Sets the branch's upstream (tracking).
Force-pushes safely, aborting if the remote has changed.

git-log.title: View commit history
git-log.description: Shows the commit history with author, date and message, from newest to oldest.
examples: One line per commit, condensed.
Visualizes branches and merges as a graph.
arguments: Compact one-line format.
Draws the branch graph.
Limits to the given number of commits.

git-diff.title: Compare changes
git-diff.description: Shows the differences between the working tree and staging, or between commits and branches.
examples: Shows changes not yet added to staging.
Shows what is already staged (will be committed).
Compares two branches.
arguments: Compares staging with the last commit.

git-show.title: Inspect a commit
git-show.description: Shows the details and diff of a specific commit, including metadata and changes.
examples: Shows the latest commit and its changes.

git-tag.title: Create tag
git-tag.description: Creates an annotated tag, usually used to mark release versions (e.g. v1.0.0).
examples: Creates an annotated tag v1.0.0.
Pushes the tag to the remote (tags aren't included in a regular push).
arguments: Creates an annotated tag (with author and message).
Tag message.

git-stash.title: Stash changes temporarily
git-stash.description: Saves uncommitted changes onto a stack and cleans the working tree, letting you switch context.
examples: Stashes the current changes.
Stashes with a description.
arguments: Includes untracked files.
Adds a message to the stash.

git-stash-pop.title: Restore stashed changes
git-stash-pop.description: Reapplies the most recent stash to the working tree and removes it from the stack.
examples: Restores and removes the latest stash.
Applies a specific stash without removing it.
arguments: Applies without removing from the stack.
warnings: May produce conflicts when reapplying onto a modified state.

git-reset-soft.title: Undo commit keeping changes
git-reset-soft.description: Removes the last commit from history but keeps its changes staged so you can recommit them.
examples: Undoes the last commit, keeping the changes staged.
arguments: Keeps the changes staged.
warnings: Alters local history; don't use on commits already pushed.

git-reset-hard.title: Discard commits and changes
git-reset-hard.description: Moves the branch to a commit and discards ALL local changes and later commits.
examples: Discards all uncommitted changes.
Forces the local branch to be identical to the remote.
arguments: Discards staging and working tree.
warnings: Rewrites local history; use git reflog to try to recover.

git-revert.title: Safely revert a commit
git-revert.description: Creates a new commit that undoes the changes of a previous commit, without rewriting history.
examples: Creates a commit that undoes the last commit.
arguments: Applies the revert without committing right away.
warnings: Ideal for shared branches, since it doesn't rewrite history.

git-reflog.title: Recover lost commits
git-reflog.description: Shows the history of where HEAD has been, letting you recover commits after a reset or rebase.
examples: Lists HEAD's previous positions.
Moves HEAD back to a state listed in the reflog.

git-cherry-pick.title: Apply a specific commit
git-cherry-pick.description: Applies the changes of a specific commit from another branch onto the current branch.
examples: Brings commit a1b2c3d into the current branch.
arguments: Records the original hash in the message.
warnings: May produce conflicts; resolve them and use git cherry-pick --continue.

git-config-user.title: Configure identity
git-config-user.description: Sets the name and email used in commits. With --global it applies to all of the user's repositories.
examples: Sets the global commit email.
Sets the name for this repository only.
arguments: Applies the setting for the current user.
Lists all active settings.

git-blame.title: Find who changed each line
git-blame.description: Shows, line by line, which commit and author last changed each part of a file.
examples: Shows the author and commit of each line in the file.
Limits to lines 10 through 20.
arguments: Restricts to a range of lines.

git-clean.title: Remove untracked files
git-clean.description: Deletes untracked files and directories from the working tree. Useful for cleaning build artifacts.
examples: Dry run: shows what would be removed, without deleting.
Actually removes untracked files and directories.
arguments: Dry run: only shows what it would remove.
Forces removal.
Includes directories.
warnings: Removes files permanently; run with -n first to check.

git-log-search.title: Search history
git-log-search.description: Finds commits that added or removed a specific string in the code (pickaxe), useful for tracing when something appeared.
examples: Lists commits that introduced or removed the word TODO.
Filters commits whose message contains 'fix'.
arguments: Searches for changes that add/remove the text.
Filters by commit message.

git-remote-set-url.title: Change remote URL
git-remote-set-url.description: Updates the address of an existing remote, for example when migrating from HTTPS to SSH.
examples: Switches origin's URL to SSH.
